title: New York and Paris as the goal; Lester Young's birthplace
summary: Waters says musicians think of New York after New Orleans, as Paris is for Europe; Lester Young's birth in Mississippi versus New Orleans is sorted out.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, I said I was goin' to Paris when I left. That's, you know, I mean, you had to - you see, it's one of those kind of things, you know, see, when you're goin' to Europe. When you go to Europe people think that it's, Paris is all of Europe. It isn't, but you know, it is, it is important city. Well, when you go to Europe that's, I think, the first thing you think of, you know. See, it's like people, musicians think of New York, you know, they don't think of no Los Angeles or not even Chicago. Kansas City wasn't so bad on account of the riverboats coming up, you know. Well, not even Chicago - it's New York that's the city. After New Orleans, we say, huh? After New Orleans, first we say New Orleans, huh? And after that is New York that the guys wanted to go, that's why they all come here, that Lester Young is born in New Orleans, but he -
That's right. New Orleans, wasn't it?
Well, he was raised for a good chunk of his childhood in New Orleans.
Oh, that I won't check on, I won't verify that -
I heard he was born in New Orleans.
'I was born in Woodville, Mississippi. I was born there and then they took me to New Orleans'.

All right - Ooooh, as a baby? (PS laughs). How about that, [ ], that's kind of technical, [ ]. OK, that's a good thing to have, [ ], I mean many people think that he's born in New Orleans. Anyway, see, but he came here to New York, you know, see. So that's where it was Paris. So I didn't go to Paris -
